chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qarashi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hurayz, from Abban ibn Taghlib, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying:

"This world will not pass away until a caller from the Heaven calls out: 'O people of the truth, gather together!' They will become in one plain. Then he will call out again: 'O people of falsehood, gather together!' They will become in one plain." I said: "Can these people enter among those people?" He said: "No, by Allah."

"And that is the word of Allah: 'Never would Allah allow the believers to remain in your condition until He separates the evil from the good. And it is not for Allah to reveal to you the unseen. But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Him, then for you is a great reward.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the people of truth and falsehood at the end of the world according to Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological separation of the faithful and the disbelievers prior to the appearance of Imam al-Qa'im, emphasizing a physical and spiritual distinctness where the two groups cannot intermingle. The cited verse from Surah Al Imran (3:179) is interpreted in Shia tradition as affirming that Allah will not leave believers in their current state of concealment or trial until He clearly distinguishes the pure from the impure, serving as a divine guarantee of the ultimate triumph of the Ahl al-Haqq.
